sources.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), pp. 1–101; complete CWI author deposit
sources.locator: Complete 101-page author-deposit PDF fetched. Read §2 Series expansions, printed pp. 3–14 (generalized hypergeometric series, the Bessel 0F1 identity, Airy series (2.14)–(2.15), and Gauss series (2.19)–(2.23)); §3 Numerical quadrature, pp. 15–43 (finite/infinite trapezoidal rules and remainder forms); §4 Recurrence relations, pp. 44–57, especially §4.1 Miller’s algorithm, pp. 48–50; and §5 Uniform asymptotic expansions, pp. 58–77.
sources.support: Independent full-text survey treatment. It supports standard series representations and recurrence/numerical-method context; the exact midpoint, interval, finite-terminal-error, and branch-enclosure claims in this batch are proved locally.

contents.name: §2, generalized hypergeometric-series framework and convergence domains, equations (2.1)–(2.9)
contents.support: Used as notation and standard-series context; the batch proves its own exact series/tail certificates.

contents.support: Supports the standard integer-order series representation; all recurrence and tail arguments are developed locally.

contents.name: §2, Airy power-series representation and initial constants, equations (2.14)–(2.15)
contents.support: Supports the standard Airy series and constants; the coefficient recurrence and tails are proved locally.

contents.name: §2.1, Gauss hypergeometric series and term recurrence, equations (2.19)–(2.23)
contents.support: The local item derives the explicit geometric tail under its stated parameter bounds.

contents.name: §3, trapezoidal-rule quadrature on finite and infinite intervals with remainder forms
contents.reason: Temme treats trapezoidal-rule remainders; this batch uses a composite midpoint rule with its own exact second-derivative estimate, so no trapezoidal theorem is imported.

contents.name: §4, two-solution recurrence theory and §4.1 Miller backward algorithm
contents.support: Temme provides recurrence-method context; the finite terminal-contamination identity and its denominator checks are proved from the local J,D solution pair.

contents.reason: The article’s §5 treats large-parameter incomplete-Gamma asymptotics; the batch makes no such claim and proves its erfcx and log-Gamma finite remainders from their own integral formulas.
